text:
Registered residential sales totaled 10,195 units valued at AED 27,672,330,524 in the last four weeks, a 6.1 percent decline in volume and 1.3 percent drop in value compared to the prior period. Mortgage registrations stood at 4,054, recorded separately from sales. The off-plan share of transactions decreased to 59.4 percent from 66.6 percent in the previous four weeks.

The median residential price per square foot fell to AED 1,666, down 1.8 percent from AED 1,697. Top performing areas by sales volume included Dubai South with 3,846 units and Jumeirah Village Circle with 2,309 units over the last twelve weeks. Business Bay recorded the highest median price at AED 2,095 per square foot, while Dubai South maintained a median of AED 1,693 per square foot.

Rental activity showed 92,516 contracts with a 50.2 percent renewal rate. The median residential rent was AED 70,000 annually. Estimated gross yields were highest in Zaabeel First at 9.1 percent for flats, followed by International City Phase 1 at 8.6 percent. Town Square, Dubai Sports City, and Dubai Production City followed with yields of 6.9, 6.6, and 6.5 percent respectively.

Price momentum varied significantly across communities. Al Yufrah 1 saw the strongest increase at 37.3 percent, while Liwan experienced the steepest decline at 14.0 percent. Palm Deira and Al Hebiah First both dropped 13.2 percent. The anomaly monitor flagged 1,073 sales in the last 60 days priced more than 35 percent away from comparable medians. Figures are based on registered DLD data and Ejari contracts, using medians and benchmark filters that exclude bulk deals, partial shares, and statistical outliers.

facts.ranking_rule: communities with at least 30 eligible sales in both 12-week windows; yields also need 30 rent contracts of the same property type
